chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Kulayb al-Asadi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

A parchment was found in the handle of the sword of the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family), in which was written: The curse of God and the angels is upon whoever initiates an offense or shelters an offender; and whoever claims (descent from) other than his (biological) father is a disbeliever in what God — Mighty and Majestic — revealed; and whoever calls (for help) to other than his patrons (people of the Religion), upon him is the curse of God.

key_terms.حَدَث: An initiated offense, typically referring to unlawful killing or creating disorder
key_terms.ذُؤَابَة: The pommel or handle-strap of a sword, where important documents were sometimes kept
key_terms.لَعْنَة: Divine curse; expulsion from divine mercy
key_terms.مَوَالِي: Patrons, allies, or people of one's religious community — those bound by bonds of walaya
key_terms.مُحْدِث: One who initiates such an offense; a perpetrator who must be brought to justice

ai.seo_question: What does the parchment found in the Prophet's sword say about cursing those who commit crimes?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) reports that a parchment was discovered in the hilt of the Prophet's sword, bearing three solemn warnings: a divine curse on those who commit or abet violent crimes, disbelief ascribed to those who disown their biological lineage (nasab), and a curse on those who seek loyalty outside their religious community. This teaching, attributed to a physical document from the prophetic era, reflects early Islamic legal norms around blood liability (diyah), the protection of lineage, and communal solidarity — all foundational concerns in classical fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Kuleyb Al Asady, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A parchment was found in the handle of a sword of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, in which was written: ‘The Curse of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Angels is upon the one who initiates an event (killing), or shelters an initiator (of a killing), and the one who claims to other than his (biological) father, so he is a disbeliever with what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed; and the one who calls (for help) to other than his friends (people of the Religion), so upon him is the Curse of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
